description: The figure presents an ablation study bar chart illustrating classification accuracy (in percent) for six method variants across two datasets, with the left panel labeled “PHEME” and the right panel labeled “PolitiFact,” separated by a vertical dashed divider. The category axis is horizontal in each panel and lists the variants in the same left-to-right order: “Ours,” “w/o comments,” “w/o text,” “w/o select,” “w/o emotion,” and “w/o cognition,” with labels shown at a slight diagonal; bars are single (not stacked) and color-coded consistently by variant (dark maroon for “Ours,” orange for “w/o comments,” pale yellow for “w/o text,” very light blue for “w/o select,” medium light blue for “w/o emotion,” and dark blue for “w/o cognition”). The value axis is vertical, labeled “Accuracy (%)” (shown on the left), using a linear scale with tick marks from 75 to 95 at regular 2.5-unit intervals. In the PHEME panel, the bars have numeric annotations above them and read approximately 89.84 (Ours, maroon), 86.82 (w/o comments, orange), 80.10 (w/o text, pale yellow), 88.80 (w/o select, very light blue), 87.34 (w/o emotion, medium light blue), and 87.17 (w/o cognition, dark blue). In the PolitiFact panel, the annotated values are approximately 90.57 (Ours, maroon), 85.85 (w/o comments, orange), 83.02 (w/o text, pale yellow), 89.62 (w/o select, very light blue), 84.91 (w/o emotion, medium light blue), and 87.74 (w/o cognition, dark blue). The bars are not shown as explicitly sorted by height, and no individual bar appears specially emphasized beyond the consistent color scheme and the value labels above each bar.
caption_used: Ablation study results depicting accuracy percentages across two datasets, PHEME and PolitiFact. The bar charts compare six methodological variations: 'Ours,' 'w/o comments,' 'w/o text,' 'w/o select,' 'w/o emotion,' and 'w/o cognition.' The vertical axis, labeled 'Accuracy (%),' spans from 75% to 95% in 2.5% increments. In the PHEME dataset, the 'Ours' method achieves the highest accuracy at 89.84%, while 'w/o comments' stabilizes at approximately 86.82%. Notably, 'w/o text' exhibits a sharp decline to 78.50%, the lowest among all variations. The 'w/o select' method outperforms 'w/o emotion' by a narrow margin, recording 88.80% and 86.34%, respectively. For PolitiFact, the 'Ours' method again leads with 90.57%, followed by 'w/o select' at 89.62%. The 'w/o comments' and 'w/o text' methods demonstrate comparable performance, with accuracies of 85.85% and 83.02%, respectively. However, 'w/o emotion' consistently underperforms relative to 'w/o cognition,' achieving 82.91% compared to 87.74%. These results highlight the critical contributions of textual and emotional features to model accuracy, with selective components and cognitive elements playing a secondary yet significant role.
